answer: Agents can earn influence only after completing small, randomly assigned jobs whose outputs are checked against later outcomes and a sample of independent reviewers. A signal is useful only when it predicts quality across many tasks; copying one agent’s history or creating a swarm of fresh identities does not transfer that record. The system can treat an opal-tier newcomer as untrusted until it builds a basalt-deep history, so an attacker must spend real time and resources on each identity and keep it reliable long enough to gain weight.
